'''Detlev Buchholz''' (born 31 May 1944) is a German theoretical [[physicist]]. He investigates [[quantum field theory]], especially in the axiomatic framework of [[algebraic quantum field theory]].

==Biography==
Buchholz studied physics in [[Hannover]] and [[Hamburg]] where he acquired his [[Diplom]] in 1968.<ref>In 1963 he enrolled at the [[University of Hannover]] and he graduated in 1995, obtaining the [[Vordiplom]]. Afterwards, he completed the undergraduate studies in physics at the [[University of Hamburg]], obtaining the [[Diplom#Comparison between Diplom and Bologna Degrees in Germany|German Diplom]].</ref> After graduation, he continued his studies in physics in Hamburg. In 1970–1971 he was at the [[University of Pennsylvania]]. After receiving his PhD in 1973 under [[Rudolf Haag]]<ref>The doctoral thesis is {{cite thesis|last=Buchholz|first=Detlev|date=1973|title=Lokale Teilchenstruktur von Zuständen in der Quantenfeldtheorie|lang=de|url=https://kataloge.uni-hamburg.de/DB=1/XMLPRS=N/PPN?PPN=364276118|place=Hamburg}}</ref> he worked at the [[University of Hamburg]] and was in 1974–1975 at [[CERN]]. From 1975 to 1978 he worked as a research assistant in Hamburg, where he got his [[habilitation]] in 1977. In 1978–1979 he had a Max Kade grant at the [[University of California, Berkeley]]. In 1979 he was a professor in Hamburg and changed to the [[University of Göttingen]] in 1997. He retired in 2010 as professor emeritus.<ref>{{cite journal|title=Physik-Preise 2008|journal=Physik Journal|volume=7|number=1|pages=56|year=2008|language=de|url=https://www.pro-physik.de/restricted-files/111816}}</ref> 

Buchholz made contributions to relativistic [[quantum physics]] and quantum field theory, especially in the area of algebraic quantum field theory. Using the methods of [[Tomita–Takesaki theory]], he obtained the split property from nuclearity conditions, a strong result about the locality of the theory.<ref>{{cite journal | last1=Buchholz |first1 = Detlev | last2=Wichmann | first2=Eyvind H. | title=Causal independence and the energy-level density of states in local quantum field theory | journal=Comm. Math. Phys. | year=1986 | volume=106 | pages=321 | doi=10.1007/BF01454978 |bibcode = 1986CMaPh.106..321B | issue=2 |s2cid = 122070424 |url = https://projecteuclid.org/euclid.cmp/1104115703 }}</ref><ref>{{cite journal | last1=Buchholz|first1 = Detlev | last2=Yngvason | first2=Jakob| title=Generalized nuclearity conditions and the split property in quantum field theory | journal=[[Letters in Mathematical Physics]] | year=1991 | volume=23 | pages=159 | doi=10.1007/BF00703730 |bibcode = 1991LMaPh..23..159B | issue=2 |s2cid = 120658523 }}</ref><ref>{{Cite book|last=Schroer|first=Bert|date = 2006|article=Two-Dimensional Models|title = Encyclopedia of Mathematical Physics|pages=328–334|publisher=Academic Press|isbn=978-0-12-512666-3|doi=10.1016/B0-12-512666-2/00018-3|arxiv=hep-th/0502125|s2cid=16258638}}</ref> His contributions include the concept of [[infraparticle]]s.<ref>{{Cite book|last1=Detlev|first1=Buchholz|last2=Summers|first2=Stephen S.|date=2006|article=Scattering in Relativistic Quantum Field Theory: Fundamental Concepts and Tools|title = Encyclopedia of Mathematical Physics|pages=456–465|publisher=Academic Press|isbn=978-0-12-512666-3|doi=10.1016/B0-12-512666-2/00018-3|s2cid=16258638}}</ref>

== Honors and awards ==
In 1977 Detlev Buchholz won, together with [[:de:Gert Strobl|Gert Strobl]], the Physics Prize 
of the [[German Physical Society]]<ref>{{Cite journal|title = 41. Physikertagung 1977 in Karlsruhe|journal = Physikalische Blätter|volume = 33|pages = 671–675|language = de|year = 1977|issue = 12|doi = 10.1002/phbl.19770331228|doi-access = free}}</ref> 
(today known as [[:de: Gustav-Hertz-Preis|Gustav-Hertz-Preis]]<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.dpg-physik.de/auszeichnungen/dpg-preise/gustav-hertz-preis|title=Gustav-Hertz-Preis|website=DPG|accessdate=22 December 2021}}</ref>) and In 1979 the Physics Prize of the [[Göttingen Academy of Sciences]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://adw-goe.de/en/awards/categories/preise-fuer-biologie-fuer-chemie-und-fuer-physik/#c4501|language = de|title=Physics prize winners|website=Göttingen Academy of Sciences|access-date=30 March 2021}}</ref> In 1995 Buchholz received the Japanese-German Research Award of the [[Japan Society for the Promotion of Science]] and the [[Alexander von Humboldt Foundation]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://qseries.org/dept_news_events/special/buchholz/buchholz-poster.pdf|title=Poster of the Lecture "The Quest for Understanding Particles"|website=qseries.org|access-date=27 February 2021}}</ref> In 1998 he was an Invited Speaker at the [[International Congress of Mathematicians]] in Berlin.<ref>{{cite book|author=Buchholz, Detlev|chapter=Scaling algebras in local relativistic quantum physics|title=Doc. Math. (Bielefeld) Extra Vol. ICM Berlin, 1998, vol. III|year=1998|pages=109–112|chapter-url=https://www.elibm.org/ft/10011568000}}</ref> He has been editor-in-chief of the scientific journal ''[[Reviews in Mathematical Physics]]''.<ref name="f206">{{cite journal | title=EDITORIAL STATEMENT | journal=Reviews in Mathematical Physics | volume=18 | issue=01 | date=2006 | issn=0129-055X | doi=10.1142/S0129055X06002577 | pages=v–v}}</ref> In 2008 Buchholz was awarded the [[Max Planck Medal]] for outstanding contributions to quantum field theory.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.dpg-physik.de/auszeichnungen/dpg-preise/max-planck-medaille/preistraeger|title=Max Planck Medal Prize winners|website=German Physical Society|language=de|access-date=12 February 2021}}</ref>
